newsitem.title: USA: Forest labs sees normal sales returning.
newsitem.headline: Forest labs sees normal sales returning.

text.p: Forest Laboratories Inc said Monday its net sales in the first quarter were $86.4 million versus $90.3 million in the 1996 quarter, attributing recent sales weakness to destocking of wholesaler inventories.
"We believe that trade inventories are now down to normal levels and that sales will now more closely reflect prescription demand for our products," said company president Howard Solomon.

Forest said net income in the first quarter ending June 30, 1997 was $0.02 per share compared with $0.47 in the comparable 1996 quarter which included a non-recurring after-tax gain of $12,687,000, or $0.27 per share.
The company said net income was $659,000 in the recent quarter compared with $21.9 million in the same quarter last year.
Solomon said improved first quarter 1997 sales compared to the two most recent quarters had allowed the company to return to profitability.
"We expect that trend to further improve in coming quarters despite the weakening prescription trends for Aerobid(R) due to heightened competition in the inhaled steroid market," he said.
"This fiscal year has already seen significant positive developments for Forest," Solomon said, including the launch of Monurol, an anbiiotic for urinary tract infection.

But the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has not yet accepted Forest's position that Infasurf should be considered a different drug from Abbott Laboratories Inc's Survanta for purposes of Orphan Drug regulations.
Forest said the agency suggested Forest perform additional studies on Infasurf for treating distress syndrome in premature infants.
The FDA has granted tentative approval for Infasurf but delayed marketing approval until the expiration of Survanta's Orphan Drug exclusivity in July 1998, Forest said.
